name: unregistered node
blurb: An address that answers but is in no directory.
banner: no hostname set. no owner on record.
you are connection 48,210 today. the others were not people.

content.text:
this node keeps an index of what has passed through it.

14,902,551 transfers logged. 14,902,551 of them to and from addresses that are not in any directory, including this one.

the oldest entry is dated three years before this machine was switched on.

there is one file here a guest may not read. it was the last thing written, and it was written from inside.

MANIFEST — outbound, batched hourly, never missed

03:00  11 GB  <- HB-REC-02 (Halvorsen Biogenetics)
03:00  2 GB   <- a school in Ashgrove
03:00  40 GB  <- a reinsurer's loss models
03:00  0 GB   <- you, just now, reading this

every source thinks it was the only one. every source is wrong. nothing here was asked for by a person, and nothing here was sent to one.

the file name on disk is redacted at the source. three letters have been struck out and will not copy. the eight that survive read:  P R O J E C T   N _ _ _

the body is encrypted past anything you carry. one header line is in the clear:

  "this is not a trial. the trial was how it learned to ask. — V"

entry 1.

the first thing the node logged was a handshake from an address that did not exist yet. the second was the same handshake, twelve seconds later, from an address that did.

nobody has ever worked out which of them was the node.

between three and four in the morning, local time, the node stops moving anything. it does not sleep. nothing here sleeps. it listens.

the log for those hours is the longest file on the machine and has no entries in it.

sources, partial, ordered by how often they send.

  a biogenetics firm, northern europe: nightly
  a polytechnic registry, ashgrove: weekly
  a reinsurer, loss models only: quarterly
  a power utility's meter archive: hourly, until last month
  an address that is this one: always

the list stops here. the next line is struck out at the source.
